why_ai: Certificated mechanics work hands-on in hangars and on ramps and personally sign return to service under Part 43, so AI can only assist the work and the paperwork.
why_clarity: Approved data and manual limits define an airworthy result, but inspection calls vary between mechanics and the truth about a borderline call can surface years later.
why_digital: Aircraft and engines come in, physical repairs and signed records go out at the airport; engine shops are bought nationally, line work locally.

why_ai: Engines are torn down, inspected and rebuilt by certificated technicians on qualified shop floors, with workscope calls worth millions and slow feedback.
why_clarity: Release standards are written, but workscopes differ by engineer and engine, and whether a build was right shows only at the next removal.
why_digital: A physical engine is shipped in and a rebuilt engine shipped back; owners routinely send engines to shops in other states or countries.

why_ai: Workscope and life-limited-part decisions are high-stakes engineering calls with signed records behind them, though the records reconciliation underneath is automatable.
why_clarity: Part lives and build rules are codified, but predicting module findings is judgement and the outcome appears at the next shop visit.
why_digital: Records, findings and quotes in, workscope plans and LLP status out on screen; owners' engineers review remotely.

why_ai: Scheduling and expediting are screen work that forecasting software increasingly does, though shop-floor constraints need people who know the floor.
why_clarity: A release date is either hit or missed within weeks, but planners re-plan differently and repair-vendor delays add noise.
why_digital: Work orders, parts status and vendor updates in, schedules and customer status reports out on screen.

why_ai: Heavy checks are weeks of hands-on inspection and structural repair on an aircraft in the hangar, signed off by certificated inspectors.
why_clarity: Routine task cards are codified, but non-routine findings vary aircraft by aircraft and their cost is known only as the check unfolds.
why_digital: The aircraft physically sits in the hangar; airlines do send aircraft abroad for heavy checks, so buying is partly national or international.

why_ai: Reading and reconciling logbooks is document work AI can largely draft, though a qualified reviewer's judgement on old entries still carries weight in a sale.
why_clarity: AD status, alteration files and time-in-service either reconcile or they don't, and reviews follow a known checklist across many aircraft.
why_digital: Paper and scanned logbooks in, a records report out; reviews are done remotely from scans as often as on site.

why_ai: A certificated mechanic must troubleshoot and sign off a transient aircraft on the ramp overnight, often on an unfamiliar type.
why_clarity: The fault either clears on the ops check or it doesn't, but transient faults vary widely by type and history.
why_digital: The aircraft is physically at that FBO tonight; the service can only be bought from a shop on the field.

why_ai: The accountable manager answers personally to the FAA for the quality system and certificate, though evidence capture and audit packs are automatable.
why_clarity: Part 145 lists the required procedures and audits test them against written manuals, with findings returned within days.
why_digital: Work orders, training and calibration records in, audit evidence out; FAA and customer audits are on site.

why_ai: Learning to maintain aircraft happens hands-on beside senior mechanics, and the result is a person authorised to sign.
why_clarity: Task lists define what must be learned, but readiness to sign alone is judged by seniors and shows in QA findings months later.
why_digital: Training happens on the hangar floor on real aircraft, with some classroom and online content.

why_ai: Matching work cards to public AD rules is text work AI can do, though an inspector still signs and carries the liability.
why_clarity: ADs follow a fixed Federal Register structure and each card either cites the current revision and method or it doesn't.
why_digital: AD texts, configuration records and work cards in, a compliance report out, all on screen.

why_ai: Drafting a compliant entry from a mechanic's words is language work AI already performs; the signature stays human.
why_clarity: A 43.9 entry has a defined structure and QA either accepts it or sends it back, thousands of times a month.
why_digital: Speech, photos and work orders in, structured records out on screen, deployed shop by shop.

why_ai: Pricing engine maintenance risk and challenging MRO invoices needs technical advisors owners trust, though cost forecasting itself is automatable.
why_clarity: Rates and invoices are measurable, but whether a rate was right is known only after the next shop visits years later.
why_digital: Invoices, workscopes and engine data in, rates and approvals out; technical advisors attend shop visits.

why_ai: Guided troubleshooting is knowledge retrieval AI does well; OEM data rights and help-desk relationships give partial protection.
why_clarity: Each fix either clears the fault or not, and fault trees are codified and repeat across a fleet.
why_digital: Fault codes and field feedback in, troubleshooting guidance out through apps and portals.

why_ai: Keeping due lists and AD status is record work AI can largely do; records custody and incumbency give the providers some protection.
why_clarity: Due dates and AD status are exact and recur across tens of thousands of aircraft, and errors surface at the next inspection.
why_digital: Logbook entries and trend data in, due lists and alerts out online, sold nationally.

why_ai: OEM engineers carry type-certificate responsibility for service bulletins and inspection programmes on products only they designed.
why_clarity: Reliability analyses follow known methods, but each in-service event is different and fixes prove out over years.
why_digital: Fleet data and teardown findings in, bulletins and reports out, with field engineers on site at operators and shops.

why_ai: Records audits are document work AI can draft, but lessors pay for named technical representatives who stand behind redelivery calls.
why_clarity: A records pack is complete or it isn't, and audits follow a repeatable checklist, though disputes settle by negotiation.
why_digital: Scanned records in, audit reports out; technical representatives attend redelivery checks in person.

why_ai: Experts testify personally in adversarial cases about maintenance standards of care, and their credibility is the product.
why_clarity: Each case is different and the answer is settled by a court or settlement long after the work.
why_digital: Wreckage, parts and records in, reports and testimony out; experts examine evidence and appear in person.

why_ai: Compiling and indexing licensed manuals and public ADs is content work AI handles; OEM licences give partial protection.
why_clarity: Libraries are current or not against AD effective dates and revision cycles, and the work repeats document by document.
why_digital: OEM documents and ADs in, an online subscription library out, sold nationally.

why_ai: Owners pay for a trusted A&P or IA advocate to argue workscopes with shops, which AI tools support rather than replace.
why_clarity: Engine-monitor analysis has codified signatures, but workscope advice varies by aircraft and outcomes show over years.
why_digital: Uploaded engine data and shop quotes in, analysis and advice out, delivered entirely remotely.

why_ai: Acquisition and integration calls are high-stakes and relationship-driven, though the modelling underneath is automatable.
why_clarity: Deal models follow known methods, but whether an acquisition paid off is known years later.
why_digital: Operating data and deal files in, models and plans out on screen, with site visits to targets.

why_ai: Building inspection AI needs physical equipment, labelled images and OEM approval, but the models themselves are software.
why_clarity: Detection accuracy is measurable against labelled images, though field truth comes from later teardowns.
why_digital: Inspection images and equipment in, software and hardware out, sold through distributors and OEM partnerships.

why_ai: Federal inspectors examine repair stations in person and take certificate actions only the government can take.
why_clarity: Surveillance follows written guidance across thousands of stations, but whether oversight prevented an accident is hard to know.
why_digital: Inspectors visit facilities and review records; findings and SDR data are published online by a single national regulator.

why_ai: Investigators examine wreckage on site and make novel causal findings with statutory authority.
why_clarity: Every accident is different and the causal finding is debated long after the event.
why_digital: Wreckage and evidence in, published reports out, from the one national investigation body.

why_ai: Cost estimates built from published programmes and rates are modelling AI can reproduce.
why_clarity: Cost per hour is a defined output updated annually, though accuracy is rarely checked against actuals.
why_digital: Published data in, an online database out, sold nationally.

why_ai: Commissioned studies and advocacy depend on member relationships; the analysis is bought in and automatable.
why_clarity: Annual reports recur on a fixed calendar, but forecasts are judged only years later.
why_digital: Member surveys in, reports and regulatory comments out, almost all digital.

why_ai: Scanning and keying records is the most automatable work in the industry once pages are captured.
why_clarity: Each page is scanned and indexed to a fixed standard at high volume with checkable results.
why_digital: Physical logbooks in, digital records out; keying is routinely done offshore.
